item.content:encoded:
Prometheus Labs as "Plunderers" is quite nice, also.

Yeah I needed a SH/WL nickname for them, and as far as I can tell there wasn't any prior art that established one, although I am actually quite split between "Plunderers" and "Pilferers". If anybody has a strong preference, please let me know!

I'd go with "Pilferers", myself. "Plunder" has the connotation of being stolen with violence, whereas Prometheus was a sneaky bugger (by necessity, violence against the gods tends to attract unwanted lightning).

• He had the rat-wizard from the PL experimental line, which let him use some sympathetic magic to let him know that they were being attacked by something made of the same stuff, he had some clues from the reading they did eariler that warned them trouble was coming, and he was able to clairvoyantly observe the attack (including the Samsara troopers' rapid healing from wounds) as it progressed.

  • Yes and also "The Witch, The Wizard and the Man of Steel", draft thread (which apparently is even slower than the fora here): http://wanderers-library.wikidot.com/forum/t-1495757/the-witch-the-wizard-and-the-man-of-steel-draft.

item.content:encoded:
I enjoyed this quite a bit. A great use of the format (and I'm biased!). Does a really good job of selling this particular god as a Thing. Lots of obviously ridiculous mythic overreach that also gets called out within the article, and undercutting via pointed Lovecraft references.

And the last line from Crow Far-Walker is incredible. Ahaha. Yesss. Best stinger.

I really like the monkey band.

(Prometheus Labs as "Plunderers" is quite nice, also.)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Considering how vague my feedback was, I have to say that I think you've implemented it perfectly ;) This version has a much more discursive feel that brings the format to life - footnote 11 was a particular highlight. And it covers the fact that this is dealing with a bunch of links and moving pieces to set up for the finale - that is now very smooth.

On a second read, I do have a few questions:

  • How does Rashid know that the Samsara squad are "immortal constructs"? Is it simply by "divin[ing] what it was that attacked us"?
  • If The Ascending Path is written in Arabic (as appears to be the case), how can Samsara squad read it?
  • Is Ulyana the Witch the same witch from "Mistakes Were Made"? My headcanon hopes so.

Maybe it's just me being jaded due to my less-than-stellar opinion of SCP-2970, but I feel this is rather by-the-numbers of a divine entity. I am largely indifferent to it, which is truly sad especially with the SH format. But still…

This is all so much bullshit. I talk with Coyote all the time and he says he was the one who stole the fire.
— Crow Far-Walker

This brought a smile to my face. I want you to know that, at least.

P.S. What's with the link to SCP-2760? Error fixed, but I dare someone to connect this with 2760.

EDIT: You know what, I don't care about this Lord of Endowments. The Doubts Section is enough reason to upvote it.
